فَارِدٌ , and its fem. (with ة): see فَرْدٌ, near the middle, in nine places: ―
-b2- and again, near the end. ―
-b3- سُكَّرٌ فَارِدٌ Sugar of the best kind, and white. (K.) ―
-b4- And إِبِلٌ فَوَارِدُ [She-camels] which stallions do not resemble (لاَ تُشْبِهُهَا). (So in the O and K. [But the right reading is evidently I think, لا تَشْتَهِيهَا, which the Turkish translator
of the K appears to have found in a copy of that work; and the meaning, therefore, which stallions do not desire. فَوَارِدُ is pl. of فَارِدَةٌ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
